chunks.text: Execution gate approval requires a planning state, readiness score, selected mode, approval lock, and run trace before any action executes.
Execution denial preserves the requested task, denial reason, operator identity, and blocked run status without executing a mutating action.
Readiness scoring separates planning confidence from execution permission and keeps unresolved requirements visible until they are classified.
Source lineage records source IDs, chunk IDs, file SHA-256 hashes, parser warnings, byte counts, and source paths for cited answer traces.
Citation validation checks that cited chunk IDs came from retrieved chunks and that source IDs remain bound to the answer trace.
Answer trace exports preserve query text, retrieval strategy, cited chunks, retrieved chunk IDs, source IDs, confidence, and validation status.
CSV ingestion inspects delimiter, headers, duplicate header warnings, row count, truncation status, and parser metadata before chunking rows.
PDF ingestion extracts text when available and keeps parser metadata, file hash, source path, byte count, and warning details.
Media ingestion for images, audio, and video is metadata-only and records file hashes plus format facts without semantic media understanding.
External directory ingestion requires an explicit directory grant before Mucaro reads files outside the project root.
Directory permission grants reject filesystem root access because broad grants weaken the local-first source boundary.
Permission revocation removes a directory grant from the local ledger and future ingest attempts must pass the permission gate again.
Persistent retrieval builds a local TF-IDF index under data indexes during ingestion and source reindex operations.
A stale persistent index is rejected when its chunk fingerprint differs from the current source chunks.
The semantic store is a local deterministic hash embedding store that rebuilds from chunks and fails closed when missing or stale.
Explicit memory remember stores operator-approved preference, profile, instruction, or fact entries in local runtime state.
Memory disable turns an item off without deleting it so active memory context excludes the disabled record.
Memory export writes all saved memory items as inspectable JSON while preserving enabled state, kind, content, and identifiers.
Tool requests create pending tool call records with tool name, arguments, reason, and audit metadata before approval.
Tool approval changes a pending call to approved and tool execution remains blocked until the approval event is recorded.
Tool denial preserves the denied call and audit event, and denied calls cannot be executed later.
CLI commands return exit code 0 for successful operations that complete their requested local workflow.
CLI commands return exit code 2 for operational failures such as missing inputs, invalid fixtures, dirty release worktrees, or failed gates.
The ask command can return exit code 3 when an answer was produced but citation validation did not report CITATION_OK.
Local release certification runs backend tests, retrieval evaluation, JSON validation, desktop package self-test, package artifact build, npm audit, and frontend build.
Fresh-clone certification clones the pushed repository, checks out an exact SHA, installs dependencies, runs release check, verifies CLI help, and smoke-tests the launcher.
Release receipt listings summarize valid and invalid receipts by type, status, bound head SHA, receipt identifier, and receipt file SHA-256.
Governed release readiness requires a successful hosted CI run for the exact current head before a governed tag is created.
GitHub startup_failure with jobs_count zero means the hosted workflow failed before GitHub created jobs or logs.
GitHub governance includes branch protection, required status checks, latest CI status, and remote tag binding for tags that point at HEAD.
Package status checks required package inputs, Python package metadata, frontend package metadata, lockfile consistency, CLI entrypoint, launcher entrypoint, and distribution blockers.
Package build writes a tracked-source ZIP plus JSON manifest with exact HEAD, archive SHA-256, member count, and per-member SHA-256.
Package build blocks dirty worktrees by default because governed release artifacts must bind to a clean source state.
Production security requires a high-entropy operator token before mutating API routes can run outside local development posture.
Production security requires explicit CORS origins so browser access is bounded to approved origins.
Public bind protection rejects non-loopback hosts unless MUCARO_AI_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND is set intentionally.
Mock mode is the deterministic default provider and supports local development without network credentials.
Live model mode requires explicit opt in, provider dependencies, and configured API credentials before live calls run.
Provider errors are returned as structured failures unless the operator explicitly allows mock fallback.
Conversation ask uses bounded prior turns as chat context while keeping source citations tied to retrieved chunks.
Deleting a conversation removes the saved chat session but keeps persisted answer traces available through run history.
Run summary counts persisted answer traces, citation OK results, citation error results, retrieval strategies, and latest run identifiers.
Retrieval fixture validation checks fixture shape, minimum size, chunk contract, query contract, and expected chunk bindings.
Retrieval fixture validation also enforces source diversity, multi-binding cases, category coverage, positive query floors, and no-context query floors.
Retrieval evaluation reports recall at k, top one hit rate, no-context accuracy, expected bindings, source IDs, multi-binding queries, and query categories.
Source delete removes the source, cascades its chunks, rebuilds the persistent index, and refreshes semantic store state.
Source reindex rebuilds persistent and semantic retrieval stores from current chunks without ingesting new files.
Schema validation reports JSON_OK with checked counts when committed JSON artifacts conform to their schemas.
The desktop launcher checks backend health, starts the app on a port, and confirms process cleanup in smoke tests.
The launcher reuses an existing healthy Mucaro backend but exits when the configured port belongs to a non-Mucaro process.
Dashboard panels show upload progress, backend health, provider labels, and runtime status for routine local operations.
